findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the sanitizer bucket and spray bottle had a low concentration of quaternary ammonium (0ppm). Went to the source of the sanitizer, the dispenser at triple sink, and it also had a low concentration (0ppm). CORRECTED: PIC discovered that the sanitizer source bottle had just become empty after use that morning. PIC had staff replace the bottle of sanitizer at the dispenser. Inspector observed that the dispenser solution had a 300ppm concentration of quat. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always at safe and effective concentration: 200 to 400 ppm for Quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the chemical dish machine (Chlorine) was not sanitizing at sufficient concentrations (no measurable sanitizer was present). Chlorine dish machines should have sanitizer concentrations between 50-200ppm. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and implement alternative ware washing procedures: dishes would be run through the dish machine for wash and rinse, and then would be finished in the triple sink sanitizing compartment which had a sanitizing concentration of 200ppm (quaternary ammonia). PIC also made plans to get a new bucket of sanitizer installed at the chemical dish machine. The PIC will send the Inspector a picture of the new bucket of sanitizer when it is installed, along with a test strip confirming the correct concentration. Ensure that chemical dish machines are sanitizing at proper concentrations, which for Chlorine is 50-200ppm, and use test strips frequently to verify the concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

During this inspection there was no verification for responsibility to report for employees. The PIC found blank copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreements in their office that had been intended for this purpose. They need to have signed copies for this prior to the follow up scheduled for 10 days.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple pots, pans and utensils throughout the facility are observed to be stored “clean” and have food debris and sticker residue remaining on them. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-washing. Education has been done with the PIC and the dish washer educated as well. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are fully cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. 

1) Two containers of yogurt in the walk in cooler are observed with use by dates that have been passed. Items expired in January 2025 and November of 2024. These items were discarded during the inspection to correct. 2) A mayonnaise based sauce in the walk in cooler is without date marking. The PIC indicated that it was from more than 7 days ago and discarded it to correct the violation. 3) RTE shrimp is observed in the walk in cooler, out of its packaging and without date marking. The PIC was shown and placed a date on it to correct. It had been opened 2 days prior to inspection.
